wine_name: Fritz Haag Brauneberger Juffer Sonnenuhr Riesling Auslese, Mosel
wrong_facts: Hook claims 60-70° slate tilt angle - not in context data and unverifiable
Hook claims 90° noon sun in October - fabricated
Hook claims 8-9 g/L racing acidity - fabricated number
Wine summary claims 6 ha amphitheater of ungrafted Riesling - ungrafted claim is almost certainly wrong (post-phylloxera Mosel vines are generally grafted), and 6 ha size is unverifiable
Wine summary claims 2018 hit 98° Oechsle, stopped at 7% abv with 92 g/L residual sugar - all fabricated numbers not in context
Wine summary claims Wilhelm Haag runs the estate - Oliver Haag has run Fritz Haag since 2005
Terroir claims 350 mm annual rainfall for Mosel - actual Mosel rainfall is ~700-750 mm annually
Terroir claims roots plunge 8-12 m - unverifiable fabrication
Vinification claims 1.2 bar pressing, 55% yield, 1,000-L fuder, 24h settling, ten months on gross lees - all fabricated specifics
Value assessment claims $65-75 US price, and specific competitor prices ($90 for von Schubert, $70 for Prüm) - no price data provided and these are fabricated
Cellar recommendation specifies 55°F, 75% RH - fabricated storage specs presented as wine-specific
reasoning: This output is extraordinarily confident and specific, but the vast majority of its numerical claims are fabricated — pH, Oechsle, residual sugar, acidity levels, vineyard size, pressing parameters, aging duration, prices, and even basic geography (350mm rainfall for Mosel is roughly half the actual figure). The hook contains multiple fabricated numbers. Calling Wilhelm Haag the current operator is wrong (it's Oliver Haag). The claim of ungrafted vines is almost certainly false. The voice is excellent — direct, opinionated, no banned words, great structure — and the specificity is maximal, but specificity without accuracy is dangerous. This is a textbook case of hallucinated precision that would destroy user trust.
